title: Symmetry of Tor for modules
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $M,N$ be $R$-modules, and let $i\ge0$. There is a natural $R$-linear isomorphism $\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(M,N)\cong\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(N,M)$, where both Tor modules are defined by the homology of a projective resolution tensored with the other module [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00M3 (lemma-tor-left-right), lines 18534-18618, including the functoriality paragraph

proof.text: Construct the tensor bicomplex of projective resolutions by [def-weil-pbc-tensor-bicomplex]. Its rows and columns are exact in positive degrees: each resolution term is projective, hence flat, and tensoring preserves the exact consecutive differentials. The zero-index cases are excluded by the positive-degree hypotheses.

Use [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-resolution-column-cokernel-iso] and [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-resolution-row-cokernel-iso] for the natural chain isomorphisms U(A)≅P tensor N and R(A)≅Q tensor M (the latter includes the factor swap). Apply the homology functor to these isomorphisms and compose with [lem-weil-pbc-double-complex-cokernel-homology-iso] and the canonical projective-resolution computations [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules] to form the components σ(M,N).

Lift f:M→M' and g:N→N' to augmentation-compatible a,b using [lem-weil-pbc-projective-resolution-lift]. The private tor_resolution_naturality combines isoLeftDerivedObj_hom_naturality and leftDerived_app_eq [lem-weil-pbc-tor-map-via-resolution-lift] to identify Tor(f,g) with H(a tensor g). Map the naturality equations of the column and row identifications through homology, invert the column equation by composing inverse isomorphisms, and use the naturality square of the double-complex comparison. Substitute these equations in the five-factor composite σ; cancel the resolution computation isomorphisms to get Tor(f,g) followed by σ(M',N')=σ(M,N) followed by Tor(g,f).
Specialize bifunctoriality to (id,g) and (f,id), simplifying identity maps. Apply NatIso.ofComponents twice to package the component isomorphisms as Tor'≅(Tor').flip.

split_report.summary: Read Stacks 00M3 (lemma-tor-left-right) with its proof, 00M1 (lemma-no-spectral-sequence), 00LS (lemma-compare-resolutions), 00LZ and Section 00LY; tags verified in tags/tags. No Mathlib declaration states Tor symmetry (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Tor.lean says Tor ≅ Tor' is not proved) and no slopmaster2 declaration states it (grep by id and key words), so the node is split. Seven steps follow the proof of 00M3: the double complex P⊗Q, exactness of rows/columns by flatness of projectives, identification of the two cokernel complexes by right exactness of ⊗, the 00M1 comparison, the swap V⊗W≅W⊗V, the composite, and the functoriality paragraph (lifts of φ, ψ, the morphism α⊗β of double complexes, the 00M1 functoriality and Tor maps via lifts). Stacks uses free resolutions; the DAG's definition uses projective ones, and only flatness and lifting are used, so the proof is written for projective resolutions (lift: new leaf lem-weil-pbc-projective-resolution-lift instead of the free-case node lem-weil-pbc-free-complex-maps-to-resolution). Remark 00M2 (signs) is not needed: any isomorphism is natural as constructed. Statement kept. New nodes: lem-weil-pbc-double-complex-cokernel-homology-iso (00M1, unsplit), lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-comm (Mathlib leaf), lem-weil-pbc-projective-resolution-lift (Mathlib leaf).
